chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sawrat ibn Kuleyb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who killed a man deliberately, and the killed one was with the right hand cut off. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If his hand was cut off during a crime which he committed against himself, or if it was cut so he took the wergild (blood money) of his hand from the one who cut it, then if his guardians intend to kill his killer, they pay to the guardians of the killer the wergild of his hand which was retaliated from; and if he had taken the wergild of his hand, and they kill him; and if they wish, they subtract the wergild of his hand from it and take the remainder.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if his hand was cut off from other than a crime he committed against himself, and a wergild was not taken by it, they kill his killer and he is not fined anything; and if they wish, they take a complete wergild.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And this is how we have found it to be in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing a person who is missing a hand?
ai.summary: This hadith, cited from the *Kitab al-Kafi*, elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of *qisas* (retaliation) and *diyah* (blood money) for a victim with a missing hand, distinguishing between disabilities incurred via prior crime versus natural causes. It highlights the scholarly principle that if the disability was compensated, heirs may deduct that value from the killer's payment, whereas uncompensated disabilities warrant full compensation. The narration concludes by anchoring these legal nuances in the authoritative *Musahaf* (or *Kitab*) of Imam Ali (AS), underscoring the continuity of prophetic legal tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin salim, from sowrat Bin Kuleyb, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a man who killed a man deliberately, and the killed one was with the right hand cut off.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘If it was such that his hand was cut off during a crime which was committed against himself, or it was cut so he took a wergild from the one who had cut it, so if his guardians (of the killed) one intend that they kill him (the killer), they can kill him and pay to the guardians of the killer a wergild of his hand which was retaliated from; even if it was that he had taken the wergild of his hand, and they kill him; and if they so desire to they subtract the wergild of his hand from it, and take the remainder’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was that his hand was cut from other than a crime committed against himself, and a wergild was not taken by it, his killer would be killed and would not be fined anything; and if they so desire to, they take the complete wergild’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And this is how we<sup>asws</sup> have found it to be in the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup>’.
